title: Mastering Crucial Conversations: The Power of Dialogue
heading: Chapter 2
chapterLocalFacts: Dialogue is modeled as both people adding facts, stories, feelings, and opinions to a shared pool.
Decisions improve when the pool is large and weaken when one or both people hold back.
Withholding usually follows a loss of safety.
The pool metaphor is intended as a portable diagnostic model.
bridgeForward: Chapter 3 turns inward and asks what the speaker wants before they contribute to the pool.

quoteLedger.text: I held back what I was actually thinking because I did not feel safe
